docs.title: GrabLab
docs.text:
Install fontlab-grablab for the grablab namespace, alongside fontlab-fontlabapp>=1.2.0. Python 3.11+ and native FontLab APIs are required for capture. Importing grablab itself is host-free; requesting Grab loads native APIs.

The retained menu scripts and native smoke example use fontlab-fly>=1.3.0 for App and native Qt access. Install Fly alongside GrabLab to run those consumers; the source installer declares it. The library-only wheel keeps App as its runtime dependency. GrabLab itself remains available through grablab.

from grablab import Grab
capture = Grab(grab_canvas=False, grab_screens=False)
capture.newGrab()
paths = capture.grabPanel("elements")

Screenshots, native widget SVG, canvas SVG/PDF, panels, menus, glyph/font windows and screen capture retain the source interfaces. An optional Grab(application=app, **preferences) reuses an existing context, useful for controlled capture and temporary preference-library paths.

Construction no longer alters rendering preferences or opens a confirmation dialog. Actual capture calls temporarily adjust OpenGL, outline thickness and pixel rendering, then restore them and the dark-glyph preference even on failure. Alternative-view exports pair their view toggles in finally blocks. Explicit setAppPrefs() applies settings directly; use capture methods for restoration. The preference library still saves GrabLab configuration when explicitly used.

A failed QImage.save returns None even when a stale target exists. Filename collisions are handled iteratively, including existing directories. Menu capture returns all submenu paths. Failed screen saves are omitted from returned artifact lists. PNG and SVG preserve title/description metadata. optimizeSVG(..., restyle=True) explicitly opts into the old font/stroke substitutions; raw capture preserves them.

# Install the sibling dependency locally (arm64 Python 3.11, as in FontLab):
uv venv --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none
uv pip install -e ../fontlab-fontlabapp -e '.[test,svg]'
./test.sh
uv build

./test.sh uses --no-sync; create the environment first. The suite covers capture, source-installer contracts and the four icon modes. Ordinary-wheel capture in FontLab 9.0.9794 verified actual Font/Glyph windows, canvas and four panels, paired metadata, DPR2 and preference restoration. Four public grabCanvas variants also passed native PNG/SVG/JSON checks; six actual Designer files passed Qt5 uic. An owned CC0 sample was closed afterward with its source unchanged. Whole-desktop capture and every panel/window configuration remain separate integration checks.

Migration provenance/licences are in MIGRATION.json; verification is in WORK.md. Versions derive from Git tags through hatch-vcs.

docs.text: Read installation, capture bundles, SVG and icons, development and limits, and licences.

docs.title: Issue 131 capture bundles
docs.text:
grabWidget, panel/window/menu captures, and standalone grabWidgetPNG / grabWidgetSVG reserve one basename across .png, .svg, .json and .ui. Image names no longer append physical pixel dimensions, so DPR 2 PNG and logical SVG stay paired. Existing image-only path list returns (and single-path methods) remain compatible; discover additive sidecars with path.with_suffix(".json") and path.with_suffix(".ui"). The enabled image formats remain configurable. A failed image or sidecar aborts the bundle; exclusive publication never replaces existing files and rolls back this capture's published members on failure.

JSON uses the FontSnap version-2 field shapes with manifest.tool="grablab" and extensions.schema="grablab.capture/1"; this describes compatibility, not FontSnap authorship or an identical capture policy. Identical records are embedded in PNG text key grablab and SVG <metadata id="grablab-metadata">. size, rects, and widget coordinates are logical units; pixels records actual PNG dimensions and dpr its device ratio. Use pixels / size per axis for fractional-scale mapping. Widget SVG-only captures leave raster measurements null.

extensions.widgets records the bounded visible QWidget hierarchy (at most 2,000 widgets), root-relative rect, parent-relative geometry, original semantic statusTip/objectName, unique XML-safe id, allowlisted control content, and local action associations. The .ui is Qt Designer XML with runtime geometry/content; JSON retains details unsuitable for Designer. Separate child windows, hidden children, models and arbitrary Qt properties are never traversed. The root may be hidden for owned test captures; descendants use isVisibleTo(root) so explicitly shown children painted by render() remain represented. Password text is omitted; other editable content is captured and may contain document data. No source code is copied from FontSnap.

Runtime capture cannot recreate layouts, signal connections, custom painting or icon resources. Original custom widget plugins are needed to load their classes. Coordinates describe widget rectangles, including portions clipped by ancestors; they do not prove pixel ownership. Directly owned named actions absent from rectangles populate context.outside; remote reaches, opener, build, theme and background stay explicitly unknown where unmeasured. Truncation and limitations are disclosed in JSON and the UI comment. Native SVG/PDF primitives retain their existing interfaces; high-level non-widget bundles are described below. Issue 131 ordinary-artifact and owned native acceptance is recorded in WORK.md.

Designer content uses writable properties for known standard controls; read-only progress/spin display text and unknown-class content remain in JSON. Numeric ranges/precision precede values, and checkable precedes the deduplicated checked property. QMenu/QMenuBar actions have their visible, nonempty rectangles measured only when wholly inside the widget and captured image; hidden/null/clipped owned actions stay outside. Designer action/addaction elements preserve supported QAction labels/state; submenu structure and signal wiring remain runtime-only.

docs.title: Screen and canvas bundles
docs.text:
grabScreens() respects the screen-selection and PNG/SVG flags, captures each chosen screen once, and publishes requested images plus one JSON sidecar under a shared basename. Its SVG embeds that same PNG in logical screen coordinates: extensions.capture_kind="screen-raster" explicitly discloses a raster-backed representation, not desktop vectorization. Actual PNG pixels/DPR and desktop geometry are retained. SVG-only still embeds a temporary PNG; it publishes no standalone PNG. grabScreenPNG retains its single PNG-path/None interface.

grabCanvas() keeps its four native workspace vector variants and optional PDF. Each enabled PNG renders the exact paired SVG through Qt QSvgRenderer into an owned QImage, with transparent initialization and guaranteed painter cleanup. extensions.capture_kind="canvas-export", source_viewBox and frame_mapping describe the native vector frame, logical dimensions and raster scale. PNG uses DPR1 at ceil(viewBox width/height); it does not claim correspondence to another editor viewport. PNG-only keeps its source SVG temporary; SVG-only skips rendering.

These non-widget captures have empty semantic records and no fabricated .ui. They reuse exclusive staged publication, collision checks and failure rollback; rendering preferences and alternative/dark toggles restore on failure. Return lists still contain only image paths (plus the existing optional PDF). Source tests alone do not qualify native behavior. The four canvas variants were also checked in FontLab 9.0.9794; whole-desktop capture remains unqualified.

docs.title: Development and limits
docs.text:
The maintained 090234b source/main and ordinary artifact milestone passed 149 tests per recorded run, with 85.12% grab and 96.65% SVG module coverage. These are source and ordinary results. The source installer now delegates the complete declared requirements to uv, including versions, markers and extras; the no-uv fallback remains presence-only. Native capture, macOS Accessibility, owner installation and script activation remain separate gates. No FontLab runtime, private historical helper or source installer is executed by this documentation build.

MIGRATION.json remains unchanged. The five retained historical helpers (copy_statusid.py, copy_statusid2.py, print_menu.py, print_uimenu.py, ui_hider.py) remain private historical/manual evidence, not newly delivered or activated scripts. Recovery does not authorize restoring them over current source.

Development uses the repository test recipe and its existing arm64 Python 3.11 host environment. Preserve the App adapter floor of 1.2.0, Fly >=1.3.0 for authored consumers, and the direct Darwin Quartz dependency declared for source installation. One runtime owns application state. See the installation and capture pages for the complete public contracts and provenance. Private Pages configuration and publication remain owner-held.

docs.title: Source installation and retained history — 2026-11-06
docs.text:
The source sdist includes the four current Scripts/GrabLab scripts and install.vfpy; the wheel installs only the library. The source installer declares App >=1.2.0, Fly >=1.3.0 for the authored consumers, and pyobjc-framework-Quartz>=10; sys_platform == 'darwin' for the macOS F5/F6 hotkey script. App's optional hotkeys extra remains available; the linked installer metadata needs the explicit Quartz requirement. See DEPENDENCIES.md for its metadata boundary.

To install into FontLab 9, open install.vfpy from a checkout in FontLab (double-click it or drop it onto FontLab), then restart FontLab. The file is a short stub that hands the work to fontlab-instamix; if instamix is not installed yet, the stub installs it from PyPI first. Instamix installs the package and its declared dependencies and records the install under the extension id com.fontlab.grablab. Owned tests do not establish native installation.

Glyph-window capture uses App's supported adapter for both direct and named-child viewports. Missing viewports raise LookupError; visibility preferences, viewport then window order, image-only returns and failure restoration remain unchanged. Current native capture is a separate acceptance surface.

Five earlier helpers remain preserved historical source, outside active Scripts and distributions, with individual dispositions:

  • copy_statusid.py: clipboard/status-ID watcher; needs owned disconnect/traversal/clipboard acceptance.
  • copy_statusid2.py: quick-help/clipboard watcher; needs separate lifecycle qualification.
  • print_menu.py: manual Markdown menu-export candidate; screenshot APIs do not replace its output.
  • print_uimenu.py: manual Designer-menu export candidate; dialog and loader state need native qualification.
  • ui_hider.py: persisted visibility/watcher prototype; needs persistence ownership and visibility/signal restoration.

Preservation does not deliver those runtime functions. No new cleanup deletion, owner installation, native acceptance or private Pages publication is qualified.

docs.title: Current English browser payload
docs.text:
The browser-component record records exact upstream notices, package archives and source maps for the theme adoption and the retained MaterialX 10.1.8 browser assets. The docs environment requires fly-january 0.4.0 or later (remote theme assets). Product terms above remain unchanged.

The English-only omission manifest binds all 35 unused lunr-languages 1.20.0 helpers, including Wordcut and TinySegmenter. The build rejects theme/search-language, corpus, vendor-set/hash and local HTML-reference drift before removing them. The manifest also records the nine local MaterialX files. docs.title: Host-free SVG processing
docs.text:
Install fontlab-grablab[svg] outside FontLab for postprocessing. Pillow decodes PNG pixels; pure-Python svgelements measures transformed SVG geometry. Neither dependency loads during native capture or ordinary import grablab.

import json
from pathlib import Path
from grablab import svg

root = svg.read_svg("panel.svg")
index = svg.build_raster_index("assets-manifest.json", source_dirs=["source-pngs"])
mapping = svg.map_images(root, index)  # JSON-serializable URI -> candidates/status
stats = {"icons": svg.process_images(root, mapping)}
stats["widgets"] = svg.tag_widgets(root, json.loads(Path("panel.json").read_text()))
svg.write_svg(root, "panel-processed.svg")  # refuses any existing output
svg.restyle(root, wireframe=True, background="white")
svg.write_svg(root, "panel-wireframe.svg")

Every data URI must match known decoded PNG dimensions and 8-bit premultiplied RGBa pixels exactly. This preserves Qt's rendered pixels despite lossy PNG unpremultiplication at translucent edges; it is not fuzzy or alpha-only matching. Index schema 2 records pixel_format="RGBa8"; rebuild older indexes before use. Candidates disclose match="pixel-exact" for exported PNG matches and match="source-name" for authoritative source PNGs associated by unique original asset name (only @2x is normalized). The latter preserves provenance but does not claim the new vector renders exactly like the old PNG. Multiple distinct SVG candidates are ambiguous and stay rasterized; unknown, unsupported and malformed images also remain untouched. Retain mapping and index JSON as receipts; paths may contain local/private information.

Nested SVGs retain image viewport/aspect ratio, ancestor transforms and clipping; local IDs, fragment/url references and CSS classes are namespaced. tag_widgets tags original elements in place using transformed bounds and the smallest containing extensions.widgets[].rect, preserving paint order and existing IDs. Equal-area ties require one proven descendant through the recorded parent chain; otherwise elements stay untagged, with sorted candidate IDs in ambiguity stats. New IDs derive from widget IDs; data-widget records the exact widget identity. Text uses its transformed anchor, disclosed by data-widget-method="text-anchor", rather than invented font metrics. Bounds containment is approximate ownership: clipping, text extents, use-instance ownership and arbitrary CSS are not inferred. Unsupported/unmatched counts and limits remain in returned stats.

compose([(path, x, y), ...], width=..., height=...) uses explicit logical positions, input paint order, source viewBox sizes and collision-free local IDs. restyle changes stroke/fill/width/background/font (system-ui by default), including inline CSS. Documents containing <mask> are refused before any mutation, including font-only changes: inherited paint and text geometry affect mask opacity. Wireframe keeps readable monochrome text and outlines on opaque surfaces. Monochrome applies a root grayscale filter, preserving luminance and existing filter effects. It refuses author stylesheets, important root filters and CSS-wide root-filter values before mutation. Wireframe alone wraps retained rasters with grayscale groups; combining rasters with author stylesheets is refused because wrapping can change selectors. Stylesheet-only vector inputs remain supported for wireframe and ordinary restyling. Image bytes/geometry remain intact; filtered_images reports the affected raster count. CSS grayscale needs a supporting SVG renderer. Ordinary color changes preserve effective none from presentation attributes, class/ID CSS and inline styles using specificity, source order, inheritance and !important. Conditional stylesheet rules and unresolved contextual paints fail before mutation. cssselect2/tinycss2 provide the selector and declaration parsing. External resources, global CSS selectors and !important rules need separate review; helpers target trusted Qt captures and the known Illustrator assets.

Optional deduplicate_paths removes only consecutive identical opaque fill-only paths without IDs, strokes or inherited opacity/effects. Repeated antialiased edges can differ; compare processed renders or leave cleanup disabled when exact pixels matter. Raw inputs remain separate. Host-free tests and asset indexing do not establish native screenshot fidelity.

docs.title: Icon representation modes
docs.text:
process_images(root, mapping=None, icon_mode="inline-svg", output=None) returns mode, linked/inlined/retained counts, retained reasons and resolved targets. The existing inline_images API is unchanged. Modes:

  • base64: retain every image without indexing assets; mapping is optional.
  • png-url: link a matching exported PNG, preferring exact pixels; ties use sorted paths. Source-name matches use the manifest's standard PNG (then the first sorted PNG variant). This is provenance, not visual equivalence.
  • svg-url: link the unique matched SVG without inserting its paths.
  • inline-svg (default): retain the existing namespaced vector substitution.

URL modes require output, the destination SVG filename, and emit escaped relative URLs to the original named assets. They do not copy/rename resources. Keep the referenced asset tree available when moving or serving the result. Both href forms are read with SVG2 href precedence; a replaced image has only href. Geometry, transforms, clipping, opacity and aspect ratio stay intact. Missing/invalid targets and ambiguous/unknown images are retained with reasons. Base64 mode preserves even malformed image URIs without decoding them. Pass output to compose as well when its directory differs from the panels; it rebases relative image URLs, preserving queries/fragments and remote URLs. These helpers target trusted Qt captures without XML base overrides.

Linked SVG interiors cannot inherit screenshot paint or font changes. Mono filters the rendered image; wireframe keeps a grayscale image rather than converting its paths. Open linked screenshots directly or use HTML iframe/object. HTML img embedding restricts external resources, so an SVG load event alone does not prove its icons loaded. See the SVG2 processing modes and image element.
